why: Rule 1: the 44.6 cm muon Braggs at its far end 15000 and cools into this deg-3 junction, where a 2.7 cm hot pi+ stub and a short e prong also emerge.
Only junction in the event; the 13.7 cm pi+ prong is hotter at its free end 3001 and the 25 cm arm runs uniformly out to the x=-200 face, but the two prongs are ~150 deg apart so I dropped a tier.
Start of the 174 cm forward muon that exits at z=500; deg-3 with two short prongs, one of which (12117) rises away and stops, and it is the most upstream point of the active region.
Rule 1 textbook: 11.5 cm proton leaves at 145k and Braggs to 188k at 10001 while the 24.5 cm muon leaves the other way and exits at z=499; prongs at 100 deg.

No degree-3 junction anywhere and all dQ/dx flat; clusters 46 and 11 lie almost collinear in the principal frame, so I took the deg-2 end 46037 (which carries a 2.3 cm stub) nearest the gap between them - close to a guess.
Rule 8 abstain: the whole event is six isolated sub-centimetre dots with no track and no readable direction anywhere, so any click would be as good as any other.
Rule 1 on a textbook stopping muon: 108 cm flat at ~50k then a monotone Bragg rise to 260k at 5001 (with a Michel-like blob 20003 4 cm off that end), so the cool start 5000 is the vertex.
Apex of a narrow 36 deg V with the charge concentrated at the apex; arm 16006 shows a clean monotone Bragg rise to 125k at its far end 16003, so that prong starts here.

In a large EM shower this is the one junction of two heavily-ionising prongs, and prong 95135 is a textbook proton - 56k leaving the vertex rising to 149k Bragg at 95153 - sitting at the upstream end of the hot core.

The chain cluster86 -> 14 -> 89100 -> 89101 -> 88098 rises monotonically to 260k at 88098, so the particle travels +y and stops there; that puts the origin at the bottom of the low-charge cluster-86 tangle, where the p5 cone opens best (+1.4 cm), but the event is diffuse.
Rule 1: the 51.9 cm muon is flat at ~50k then Braggs monotonically to 145k at 17001, and the pi+/proton chain leaves this deg-2 junction the other way at ~97 deg.

Rule 1 at its strongest - 2 of 2 prongs rise away (x3.79, x2.40) with a genuine monotone Bragg at both far ends on p4 - but the prong pair is 169 deg apart, and two fitted tracks glued end-to-end would look exactly like this, so I took the mandated tier drop.

Chosen over 6003 (8 cm away, zoom checked) because it is the only reading that gives the 72 cm heavily-ionising track an origin, and it carries by far the densest charge in the event; rule 1 formally opposes it (0 of 2 rise away) since that dense end could equally be where that track stops, so this is close to a coin flip.

The 123 cm track shows a monotone 6 cm Bragg decline read into 18000 (it stops there) and only a single-bin blob at 18002, so rule 1 puts the vertex at the cool upstream end 18002, which is also the lower-z end.
Classic CC topology at the most upstream candidate (z=26): an 86 cm muon Bragging at 17000 and an 83 cm proton Bragging at 174k at 17008 both leave this deg-3 vertex at ~86 deg, plus a 2.4 cm stub.
